question: Let \(\mathcal{R}\) be the region in the complex plane consisting of all complex numbers \(z\) that can be written as the sum of complex numbers \(z_1\) and \(z_2,\) where \(z_1\) lies on the segment with endpoints \(3\) and \(4i,\) and \(z_2\) has magnitude at most \(1.\) What integer is closest to the area of \(\mathcal{R}?\)
solution:
For each fixed \(z_1\), adding every complex number of magnitude at most \(1\) fills a disk of radius \(1\) centered at \(z_1\). This lets us describe the region geometrically.

Indeed, \(z=z_1+z_2\) with \(|z_2|\le1\) is equivalent to \(|z-z_1|\le1\). Thus \(\mathcal R\) consists exactly of the points within distance \(1\) of the segment joining \(A=(3,0)\) and \(B=(0,4)\). The segment has length
\[
AB=\sqrt{(3-0)^2+(0-4)^2}=5.
\]

To determine the shape, consider the perpendicular projection of a point onto the line \(AB\). If the projection lies on the segment, that projection is the nearest point of the segment. These points form a rectangle of length \(5\) and width \(2\). Beyond either endpoint, the nearest point of the segment is that endpoint, giving an outward semicircle of radius \(1\).

The rectangle and the two semicircles meet only along their boundaries, so their areas add:
\[
\operatorname{Area}(\mathcal R)
=5\cdot2+2\left(\frac12\pi\cdot1^2\right)
=10+\pi\approx13.14.
\]
The closest integer is \(\boxed{13}\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
